subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept this policy-active Codex path after `code_mode_exec` is normalized to `exec`, including the unified-exec runtime prerequisite and fresh-thread behavior on relay config fingerprint changes?
rationale: The mechanical shell-policy alias is clear, but accepting a patched Codex runtime dependency plus availability/session tradeoffs for policy-active turns is a security and compatibility boundary decision.

options.title: Repair alias, then accept tradeoff
options.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec` through `exec`, keep the scoped unified-exec and binding changes, and proceed only after owner review of the security and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Hold for upstream runtime contract
options.body: Pause until the Codex runtime contract for outer Code Mode PreToolUse delivery is present in upstream and can be proven without relying on local patched behavior.

options.title: Prefer fail-closed canary path
options.body: Close or supersede this branch in favor of a fail-closed approach such as #90805 if maintainers do not want to depend on positive Code Mode hook delivery yet.

recommendation.title: Repair alias, then accept tradeoff
recommendation.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec` through `exec`, keep the scoped unified-exec and binding changes, and proceed only after owner review of the security and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history shows repeated work on the Codex/native hook relay path and this owner is a good routing point for the compatibility/security decision.
